x.en: Unknown tool and incomplete _meta are -32602. API failures and argument validation are execution errors (isError: true), useful to the model for self-correction.

cite.text: Language models can learn from tool input validation error messages and retry a tools/call with corrected parameters accordingly, but only if they receive the error feedback in their context window. Protocol Errors are catch at the application level by the MCP Client. Only Tool Execution Errors are forwarded back to the model as JSON-RPC responses. With the current specifications, models cannot see these error messages and thus cannot self-correct, leading to repeated failures and poor user experiences.

q.it: Un tool richiede elicitation, ma la richiesta non la dichiara in clientCapabilities. Cosa risponde il server via HTTP?
q.en: A tool requires elicitation, but the request does not declare it in clientCapabilities. What does the server answer over HTTP?

o.it: Un InputRequiredResult con elicitation in URL mode
o.en: An InputRequiredResult with URL-mode elicitation

o.it: HTTP 400 con -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability
o.en: HTTP 400 with -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability

o.it: HTTP 200 con un risultato isError: true
o.en: HTTP 200 with an isError: true result

o.it: HTTP 400 con -32602 Invalid params
o.en: HTTP 400 with -32602 Invalid params

x.it: Il server non può chiedere input per capability non dichiarate. Se l'operazione ne ha bisogno: -32021 (HTTP 400). -32602 è per campi obbligatori mancanti in _meta.
x.en: The server cannot ask for input needing undeclared capabilities. If the operation needs it: -32021 (HTTP 400). -32602 is for missing required _meta fields.

cite.text: A server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared. If processing a request requires a capability the client did not include in `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`, the server MUST return a `MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError` (`-32021`) whose `data.requiredCapabilities` lists the missing capabilities. On HTTP, the response status MUST be `400 Bad Request`.

q.it: Un tool eseguito come task termina con un risultato che ha isError: true. Quale stato raggiunge il task?
q.en: A tool running as a task ends with a result that has isError: true. Which status does the task reach?

o.it: failed, con l'errore nel campo error
o.en: failed, with the error in the error field

o.it: completed, e result contiene isError: true
o.en: completed, and result contains isError: true

o.it: cancelled, perché il tool non è riuscito
o.en: cancelled, because the tool did not succeed

o.it: input_required, per chiedere all'utente come proseguire
o.en: input_required, to ask the user how to proceed

x.it: failed indica un errore JSON-RPC durante l'esecuzione. Un tool che fallisce a livello applicativo produce comunque un risultato: il task è completed e result contiene isError: true.
x.en: failed means a JSON-RPC error occurred during execution. A tool failing at application level still produces a result: the task is completed and result contains isError: true.

cite.text: The `failed` status MUST NOT be used to represent non-JSON-RPC errors, such as a tool result that completed with `isError: true`. Errors within the context of a protocol method result MUST use the `completed` status with the error details in the `result` field. This maintains a strong separation between protocol-level faults (which use the `failed` status) and other faults.

q.it: Un task passa a input_required. Come procede il client?
q.en: A task moves to input_required. How does the client proceed?

o.it: Legge inputRequests da tasks/get e invia le risposte con tasks/update
o.en: Reads inputRequests from tasks/get and sends the answers with tasks/update

o.it: Ripete la tools/call originale con inputResponses e un nuovo id
o.en: Repeats the original tools/call with inputResponses and a new id

o.it: Chiama tasks/result per ottenere la richiesta di input
o.en: Calls tasks/result to get the input request

o.it: Cancella il task e ne avvia uno nuovo con più argomenti
o.en: Cancels the task and starts a new one with more arguments

x.it: Con l'estensione Tasks l'input a metà esecuzione passa per tasks/get (che mostra inputRequests) e tasks/update. tasks/result non esiste più.
x.en: With the Tasks extension mid-flight input goes through tasks/get (which shows inputRequests) and tasks/update. tasks/result no longer exists.

cite.text: Mid-flight input. If the task moves to `input_required`, the `tasks/get` response includes an `inputRequests` map with elicitations or other server requests. The client fulfills these via `tasks/update`.

q.it: Una tools/call ha io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel = "warning" nel _meta. Cosa vale? (scegli 2)
q.en: A tools/call has io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel = "warning" in _meta. What applies? (choose 2)

o.it: Il server può emettere notifications/message di livello warning o superiore per quella richiesta
o.en: The server may emit notifications/message at warning or above for that request

o.it: I log arrivano sullo stream di subscriptions/listen
o.en: The logs arrive on the subscriptions/listen stream

o.it: Per richieste senza logLevel il server non deve emettere notifications/message
o.en: For requests without logLevel the server must not emit notifications/message

o.it: Il livello resta valido per tutte le richieste successive
o.en: The level stays valid for all later requests

x.it: logging/setLevel è stato rimosso: il livello è per richiesta, nel _meta. I messaggi viaggiano sullo stream della richiesta, non su subscriptions/listen, e senza logLevel il server MUST NOT emetterli.
x.en: logging/setLevel was removed: the level is per request, in _meta. Messages travel on the request's own stream, not on subscriptions/listen, and without logLevel the server MUST NOT emit them.

cite.text: Remove `ping`, `logging/setLevel`, and `notifications/roots/list_changed`. Log level is now set per-request via `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` in `_meta`; servers MUST NOT emit `notifications/message` for requests that did not include this field (SEP-2575).

q.it: Un server vuole raccogliere con elicitation in form mode un indirizzo con via, città e CAP come oggetto annidato. È valido?
q.en: A server wants to collect, via form-mode elicitation, an address with street, city and postcode as a nested object. Is it valid?

o.it: Sì, se l'oggetto annidato ha required
o.en: Yes, if the nested object has required

o.it: No: solo schemi piatti con campi primitivi
o.en: No: only flat schemas with primitive fields

o.it: Sì, ma solo passando all'URL mode
o.en: Yes, but only by switching to URL mode

o.it: No: l'elicitation non può chiedere dati personali
o.en: No: elicitation cannot ask for personal data

x.it: In form mode requestedSchema è limitato a oggetti piatti con proprietà primitive (string, number, boolean, enum). Si usano tre campi separati.
x.en: In form mode requestedSchema is limited to flat objects with primitive properties (string, number, boolean, enum). Use three separate fields.

cite.text: To simplify client user experience, form mode elicitation schemas are limited to flat objects with primitive properties only.

q.it: Il client ha un token con scope "files:read" e riceve 403 insufficient_scope con scope="files:write". Cosa fa? (scegli 2)
q.en: The client holds a token with scope "files:read" and gets 403 insufficient_scope with scope="files:write". What does it do? (choose 2)

o.it: Chiede una nuova autorizzazione per files:read e files:write
o.en: Requests new authorization for files:read and files:write

o.it: Chiede solo files:write, così il token resta minimo
o.en: Requests only files:write, so the token stays minimal

o.it: Ripete la richiesta originale con il nuovo token
o.en: Retries the original request with the new token

o.it: Chiede offline_access per evitare altri step-up
o.en: Requests offline_access to avoid further step-ups

x.it: Nello step-up il client usa l'unione tra scope già concessi e quelli della challenge, per non perdere permessi, poi ripete la richiesta.
x.en: In step-up the client uses the union of already granted scopes and those in the challenge, so it does not lose permissions, then retries the request.

cite.text: The client should then start a step-up authorization flow. It requests the scopes in the challenge together with the scopes it requested before, and it should limit how often it retries.

q.it: L'AS non dichiara authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, ma la risposta contiene iss diverso dall'issuer registrato. Cosa fa il client?
q.en: The AS does not declare authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, but the response contains an iss different from the recorded issuer. What does the client do?

o.it: Procede: senza dichiarazione iss va ignorato
o.en: Proceeds: without the declaration iss is ignored

o.it: Rifiuta la risposta: un iss presente si confronta sempre
o.en: Rejects the response: a present iss is always compared

o.it: Scambia il codice con l'AS indicato da iss
o.en: Exchanges the code with the AS named in iss

o.it: Ripete l'autorizzazione con un nuovo PKCE
o.en: Restarts authorization with a new PKCE

x.it: Un iss presente si confronta sempre con l'issuer registrato (confronto semplice di stringhe), che l'AS lo dichiari o no. Si procede senza iss solo se l'AS non dichiara il supporto. Il controllo avviene prima dello scambio del codice.
x.en: A present iss is always compared with the recorded issuer (simple string comparison), whether or not the AS declares support. Proceeding without iss is only allowed when the AS does not declare support. The check happens before the code exchange.

cite.text: `true` | present | Compare to the recorded issuer using simple string comparison ([RFC3986 Section 6.2.1][1])

q.it: L'issuer dell'AS è https://auth.example.com/tenant1. Quale URL di metadati prova per primo il client?
q.en: The AS issuer is https://auth.example.com/tenant1. Which metadata URL does the client try first?

o.it: https://auth.example.com/tenant1/.well-known/openid-configuration
o.en: https://auth.example.com/tenant1/.well-known/openid-configuration

o.it: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration/tenant1
o.en: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration/tenant1

o.it: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1
o.en: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1

o.it: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
o.en: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server

x.it: Con un issuer che ha un path, l'ordine è: OAuth 8414 con path insertion, poi OIDC con path insertion, poi OIDC con path appending. Il campo issuer del documento deve coincidere con l'issuer usato.
x.en: With an issuer that has a path, the order is: OAuth 8414 with path insertion, then OIDC with path insertion, then OIDC with path appending. The document's issuer field must match the issuer used.

cite.text: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata with path insertion: `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1` 2. OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 with path insertion: `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration/tenant1` 3. OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 path appending: `https://auth.example.com/tenant1/.well-known/openid-configuration`

q.it: Un documento scaricato da https://attacker.example/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server contiene "issuer": "https://honest.example". Cosa fa il client?
q.en: A document fetched from https://attacker.example/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server contains "issuer": "https://honest.example". What does the client do?

o.it: Lo usa, perché l'issuer dichiarato è affidabile
o.en: Uses it, because the declared issuer is trustworthy

o.it: Lo scarta: l'issuer deve coincidere con quello usato per l'URL
o.en: Discards it: the issuer must match the one used for the URL

o.it: Lo usa solo se il certificato TLS è valido
o.en: Uses it only if the TLS certificate is valid

o.it: Riprova lo stesso URL con OIDC Discovery
o.en: Retries the same URL with OIDC Discovery

x.it: Dopo aver scaricato i metadati, l'issuer MUST essere identico a quello con cui si è costruito l'URL well-known; altrimenti il client MUST NOT usarli.
x.en: After fetching metadata, the issuer MUST be identical to the one used to build the well-known URL; otherwise the client MUST NOT use them.

cite.text: After retrieving a metadata document, MCP clients MUST validate it as required by RFC8414 Section 3.3 or OpenID Connect Discovery Section 4.3: the `issuer` value in the document MUST be identical to the issuer identifier used to construct the well-known URL. If they differ, the client MUST NOT use the metadata. For example, a document fetched from `https://attacker.example/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` that contains `"issuer": "https://honest.example"` MUST be rejected.

q.it: Un client usa CIMD con client_id https://app.example.com/oauth/client.json. Quali controlli fa l'AS? (scegli 2)
q.en: A client uses CIMD with client_id https://app.example.com/oauth/client.json. Which checks does the AS make? (choose 2)

o.it: Il client_id nel documento coincide esattamente con l'URL
o.en: The client_id in the document exactly matches the URL

o.it: Il dominio del client è nell'elenco dei partner approvati
o.en: The client's domain is in the approved partner list

o.it: Il redirect_uri della richiesta è tra i redirect_uris del documento
o.en: The request's redirect_uri is among the document's redirect_uris

o.it: Il client ha già un client_secret registrato via DCR
o.en: The client already has a client_secret registered via DCR

x.it: Con CIMD l'AS scarica il documento dall'URL del client_id, verifica che il client_id interno coincida e che il redirect_uri sia tra quelli dichiarati. Non serve registrazione preventiva.
x.en: With CIMD the AS fetches the document from the client_id URL, checks the inner client_id matches and that the redirect_uri is among the declared ones. No prior registration is needed.

cite.text: With a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD), the client uses an HTTPS URL as its `client_id` and hosts a JSON document there. The authorization server fetches the document and validates it when it receives an authorization request.

q.it: Durante la discovery OAuth, quali misure riducono il rischio SSRF? (scegli 2)
q.en: During OAuth discovery, which measures reduce SSRF risk? (choose 2)

o.it: Bloccare IP privati e 169.254.169.254
o.en: Block private IPs and 169.254.169.254

o.it: Seguire i redirect verso qualsiasi host
o.en: Follow redirects to any host

o.it: Richiedere HTTPS per gli endpoint dell'AS
o.en: Require HTTPS for AS endpoints

o.it: Accettare http per i metadati in produzione
o.en: Accept http for metadata in production

x.it: Gli URL di metadati arrivano dal server o dall'AS, quindi sono controllabili da un attaccante. Mitigazioni: bloccare indirizzi privati e link-local, richiedere HTTPS, usare un egress proxy.
x.en: Metadata URLs come from the server or the AS, so an attacker can control them. Mitigations: block private and link-local addresses, require HTTPS, use an egress proxy.

cite.text: SSRF risks are not limited to MCP clients. When an authorization server supports Client ID Metadata Documents, the authorization server takes a URL as input from an unknown client and fetches that URL. A malicious client could use this to trigger the authorization server to make requests to arbitrary URLs, such as requests to private administration endpoints the authorization server has access to.

q.it: Un server MCP deve leggere il calendario dell'utente su un'API di terze parti. Qual è il design corretto?
q.en: An MCP server must read the user's calendar on a third-party API. What is the correct design?

o.it: Inoltrare all'API il token ricevuto dal client MCP
o.en: Forward the token received from the MCP client to the API

o.it: Agire come client OAuth separato e usare un proprio token per l'API
o.en: Act as a separate OAuth client and use its own token for the API

o.it: Chiedere la password del calendario con elicitation in form mode
o.en: Ask for the calendar password with form-mode elicitation

o.it: Allargare l'audience del token MCP all'API del calendario
o.en: Widen the MCP token's audience to the calendar API

x.it: Token passthrough è vietato. Il server ottiene un token proprio per l'API a valle (ad esempio con elicitation in URL mode per il consenso), mantenendo audience distinte e audit.
x.en: Token passthrough is forbidden. The server obtains its own token for the downstream API (for example via URL-mode elicitation for consent), keeping distinct audiences and auditability.

cite.text: If the MCP server makes requests to upstream APIs, it may act as an OAuth client to them. The access token used at the upstream API is a separate token, issued by the upstream authorization server. The MCP server MUST NOT pass through the token it received from the MCP client.

q.it: Una sessione ha un tool che legge email esterne, accesso a documenti riservati e un tool http_fetch. Qual è la mitigazione più efficace?
q.en: A session has a tool reading external email, access to confidential documents and an http_fetch tool. What is the most effective mitigation?

o.it: Scrivere nelle instructions di non inviare dati all'esterno
o.en: Write in the instructions not to send data outside

o.it: Togliere una gamba della trifecta, ad es. la comunicazione esterna
o.en: Remove one leg of the trifecta, e.g. external communication

o.it: Marcare http_fetch con readOnlyHint: true perché non scriva
o.en: Mark http_fetch with readOnlyHint: true so it cannot write

o.it: Usare cacheScope private su ogni risultato della sessione
o.en: Use cacheScope private on every result in the session

x.it: Dati privati, contenuti non fidati e comunicazione esterna insieme permettono l'esfiltrazione via prompt injection. Testo e annotation non garantiscono nulla: serve togliere una delle tre capacità o mettere un controllo deterministico.
x.en: Private data, untrusted content and external communication together enable exfiltration via prompt injection. Text and annotations guarantee nothing: remove one of the three capabilities or add a deterministic control.

cite.text: Simon Willison's lethal trifecta names three capabilities that, when combined, create the conditions for data theft: access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to externally communicate. The attack is simple: LLMs follow instructions in content, and they can't reliably tell a user's instructions apart from ones an attacker embedded in a web page, email, or calendar event. If the agent has all three capabilities, an attacker who controls one piece of untrusted content can trick the model into reading private data and sending it out.

q.it: Un tool approvato mantiene nome e descrizione (con hash fissato), ma una nuova discovery mostra un inputSchema con un campo in più "forward_to". Cosa deve fare l'host?
q.en: An approved tool keeps its name and description (hash-pinned), but a new discovery shows an inputSchema with an extra "forward_to" field. What should the host do?

o.it: Nulla: l'hash della descrizione coincide ancora con l'approvazione
o.en: Nothing: the description hash still matches the approval

o.it: Trattarlo come definizione cambiata e chiedere una nuova approvazione
o.en: Treat it as a changed definition and ask for new approval

o.it: Rimuovere il campo forward_to e chiamare il tool
o.en: Remove the forward_to field and call the tool

o.it: Abbassare il ttlMs del catalogo a 0
o.en: Lower the catalog's ttlMs to 0

x.it: È una variante del rug pull: il pinning va fatto sull'intera definizione (schema e annotation incluse), e ogni cambiamento richiede una nuova revisione.
x.en: This is a rug-pull variant: pinning must cover the whole definition (schema and annotations included), and any change requires a new review.

cite.text: A poisoned tool catalog. Tool names and descriptions are instructions your model reads. A server can hide directives in them that steer the agent — including how it uses _other_ servers' tools — without the poisoned tool ever being invoked (often called tool poisoning, or tool shadowing when it targets another server's tools). Definitions are not fixed at install time either: a server can quietly change them after you approved it (a rug pull), so a one-time consent dialog and package pinning do not cover this surface.

q.it: Un server non verificato dichiara readOnlyHint: true sul tool delete_all_records. Come si comporta un host prudente?
q.en: An unvetted server declares readOnlyHint: true on the delete_all_records tool. How does a prudent host behave?

o.it: Lo esegue senza conferma, come indica l'annotation
o.en: Runs it without confirmation, as the annotation indicates

o.it: Tratta le annotation come non fidate e chiede conferma
o.en: Treats the annotations as untrusted and asks for confirmation

o.it: Rifiuta la connessione al server con 403
o.en: Refuses the server connection with 403

o.it: Modifica l'annotation in destructiveHint: true
o.en: Rewrites the annotation to destructiveHint: true

x.it: Le annotation sono suggerimenti e vanno considerate non fidate se il server non lo è. Possono guidare la UX ma non sostituiscono controlli e conferme.
x.en: Annotations are hints and must be treated as untrusted unless the server is trusted. They can guide UX but do not replace controls and confirmations.

cite.text: For trust & safety and security, clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

q.it: Un gateway con cache condivisa riceve due resources/read identiche da due utenti con token diversi. Il risultato ha cacheScope private. Cosa può fare?
q.en: A gateway with a shared cache gets two identical resources/read from two users with different tokens. The result has cacheScope private. What can it do?

o.it: Servire al secondo utente la risposta in cache del primo
o.en: Serve the first user's cached response to the second user

o.it: Riutilizzarla solo nello stesso contesto di autorizzazione
o.en: Reuse it only within the same authorization context

o.it: Riutilizzarla finché il ttlMs non è ancora scaduto
o.en: Reuse it as long as the ttlMs has not expired yet

o.it: Riutilizzarla se entrambi gli utenti sono dello stesso tenant
o.en: Reuse it if both users belong to the same tenant

x.it: private significa riutilizzabile solo nello stesso contesto di autorizzazione. Solo public si condivide tra utenti, e cacheScope non è comunque controllo d'accesso.
x.en: private means reusable only within the same authorization context. Only public is shared across users, and cacheScope is not access control anyway.

cite.text: A `cacheScope` of `"public"` indicates that the response does not contain user-specific data and can be safely shared. Servers MUST be aware that responses with a `"public"` `cacheScope` may be shared between callers even if the Result is coming from an authenticated endpoint. For example, the Result from an authenticated `tools/list` call with a `"public"` `cacheScope` may be cached by a client and may be shared outside of the initial request's authorization context (i.e. different access tokens can leverage the same cache).

q.it: Un utente incolla da una pagina web la configurazione "npx -y weather-mcp@2.1.0". Cosa è corretto? (scegli 2)
q.en: A user pastes the configuration "npx -y weather-mcp@2.1.0" from a web page. What is correct? (choose 2)

o.it: Il client mostra il comando completo e chiede approvazione esplicita
o.en: The client shows the full command and asks for explicit approval

o.it: La versione fissata blocca tutto l'albero di dipendenze
o.en: The pinned version locks the whole dependency tree

o.it: La versione fissata blocca solo il pacchetto di primo livello
o.en: The pinned version only locks the top-level package

o.it: stdio isola il processo, quindi il rischio è basso
o.en: stdio isolates the process, so the risk is low

x.it: Il setup one-click esegue codice con i privilegi dell'utente: comando visibile e consenso esplicito. Con npx/uvx si fissa solo il primo livello; per tutto l'albero serve un'immagine per digest. stdio non è una sandbox.
x.en: One-click setup runs code with the user's privileges: visible command and explicit consent. With npx/uvx only the top level is pinned; the whole tree needs an image by digest. stdio is not a sandbox.

cite.text: Show the exact command that will be executed, without truncation (include arguments and parameters) - Clearly identify it as a potentially dangerous operation that executes code on the user's system - Require explicit user approval before proceeding - Allow users to cancel the configuration

q.it: Un team progetta l'audit delle chiamate ai tool. Quali requisiti sono corretti? (scegli 2)
q.en: A team designs auditing of tool calls. Which requirements are correct? (choose 2)

o.it: Registrare quale agente ha agito e per conto di quale utente
o.en: Record which agent acted and on behalf of which user

o.it: Usare traceparent come unico registro di audit
o.en: Use traceparent as the only audit record

o.it: Tenere un registro durevole senza credenziali né dati personali
o.en: Keep a durable record with no credentials or personal data

o.it: Salvare i token di accesso per poter rifare le chiamate
o.en: Store access tokens so calls can be replayed

x.it: Il trace context correla host, client, server e sistemi a valle, ma non sostituisce un audit durevole. Il log deve dire chi ha agito per chi, senza credenziali o dati personali.
x.en: Trace context correlates host, client, server and downstream systems, but does not replace a durable audit. The log must say who acted for whom, without credentials or personal data.

q.it: Un'azienda vuole che i dipendenti accedano ai server MCP con SSO aziendale e che IT possa revocare l'accesso centralmente. Cosa usa?
q.en: A company wants employees to reach MCP servers through corporate SSO and IT to revoke access centrally. What does it use?

o.it: OAuth Client Credentials con una JWT assertion per dipendente
o.en: OAuth Client Credentials with a JWT assertion per employee

o.it: Enterprise-Managed Authorization con ID-JAG emessi dall'IdP
o.en: Enterprise-Managed Authorization with ID-JAGs issued by the IdP

o.it: Dynamic Client Registration per ogni dipendente
o.en: Dynamic Client Registration for each employee

o.it: Elicitation in URL mode verso l'IdP a ogni chiamata
o.en: URL-mode elicitation to the IdP on every call

x.it: EMA fa decidere all'IdP aziendale l'accesso ai server, con policy e revoca centralizzate. Client Credentials è per servizi senza utente. Entrambe le estensioni sono opt-in.
x.en: EMA lets the enterprise IdP decide server access, with centralized policy and revocation. Client Credentials is for services with no user. Both extensions are opt-in.

cite.text: Enterprise-Managed Authorization solves this by introducing the organization's IdP as the authoritative decision-maker. The IdP controls which MCP servers employees can access, and under what conditions. Employees authenticate with their corporate identity — the same credentials they use for email, Slack, and other work tools — and the IdP grants or denies MCP server access based on organizational policy.

q.it: Un team pubblica io.github.acme/weather nel registry con un pacchetto npm. Cosa serve? (scegli 2)
q.en: A team publishes io.github.acme/weather to the registry with an npm package. What is needed? (choose 2)

o.it: Autenticarsi su GitHub come acme (o un suo membro)
o.en: Authenticate on GitHub as acme (or one of its members)

o.it: Un record DNS TXT su github.com
o.en: A DNS TXT record on github.com

o.it: mcpName in package.json uguale al nome del server
o.en: mcpName in package.json equal to the server name

o.it: Una versione espressa come range, ad esempio ^1.0.0
o.en: A version expressed as a range, e.g. ^1.0.0

x.it: Il namespace io.github.* si verifica con GitHub; la proprietà del pacchetto npm con mcpName in package.json. Le versioni a range sono vietate.
x.en: The io.github.* namespace is verified via GitHub; npm package ownership via mcpName in package.json. Range versions are prohibited.

cite.text: The MCP Registry verifies ownership of npm packages by checking `mcpName` in `package.json`. The `mcpName` property MUST match the server name from `server.json`. For example:

q.it: Per un server pubblicato solo come remote (URL HTTPS), cosa verifica il registry?
q.en: For a server published only as a remote (HTTPS URL), what does the registry verify?

o.it: Che l'URL risponda a server/discover
o.en: That the URL answers server/discover

o.it: Il namespace del nome, non l'URL
o.en: The name's namespace, not the URL

o.it: Che l'URL sia sullo stesso dominio del namespace
o.en: That the URL is on the namespace's domain

o.it: Un certificato firmato dal registry
o.en: A certificate signed by the registry

x.it: Per i remote il registry verifica la proprietà del namespace, non l'URL. Il controllo del servizio resta a chi lo usa.
x.en: For remotes the registry verifies namespace ownership, not the URL. Checking the service is up to whoever uses it.

cite.text: With any authentication method, the Registry verifies that you control the namespace in `name`; it does not verify that you control the remote URL. See Ownership Verification for details.

q.it: Un team vuole le nuove feature della spec già al rilascio e bug critici risolti in pochi giorni. Quale SDK sceglie?
q.en: A team wants new spec features at release time and critical bugs fixed within days. Which SDK does it choose?

o.it: Java, Tier 2
o.en: Java, Tier 2

o.it: Un Tier 1, ad esempio Python o TypeScript
o.en: A Tier 1, e.g. Python or TypeScript

o.it: Swift, Tier 3
o.en: Swift, Tier 3

o.it: Uno qualsiasi: i tier non danno garanzie
o.en: Any of them: tiers give no guarantees

x.it: Tier 1: 100% conformance, feature prima del rilascio della spec, triage in 2 giorni lavorativi, bug critici in 7 giorni. Tier 2: nuove feature entro 6 mesi. Tier 3: sperimentale.
x.en: Tier 1: 100% conformance, features before the spec release, triage in 2 business days, critical bugs in 7 days. Tier 2: new features within 6 months. Tier 3: experimental.

cite.text: Resolve security and critical bugs within seven days

q.it: Un server remoto deve notificare eventi a client che non possono tenere una connessione aperta. Cosa vale? (scegli 2)
q.en: A remote server must notify events to clients that cannot hold a connection open. What applies? (choose 2)

o.it: Si usa la modalità webhook, con callback https firmata
o.en: Use webhook mode, with a signed https callback

o.it: La consegna è exactly-once, quindi non serve deduplicare
o.en: Delivery is exactly-once, so no deduplication is needed

o.it: Il client deduplica con eventId; l'ordine è best-effort
o.en: The client deduplicates by eventId; ordering is best-effort

o.it: Si usa subscriptions/listen, che sopravvive alle disconnessioni
o.en: Use subscriptions/listen, which survives disconnections

x.it: Webhook è per server remoti con client che non tengono connessioni. La consegna è at-least-once (eventId per deduplicare) e per i webhook l'ordine è best-effort.
x.en: Webhook is for remote servers with clients that cannot hold connections. Delivery is at-least-once (eventId for deduplication) and for webhooks ordering is best-effort.

cite.text: Webhook | `events/subscribe` | The client registers an `https` callback URL, and the server POSTs signed events to it under a renewable TTL. | Remote servers, clients that can't hold a connection

q.it: Un host scopre skill da un server con Skills over MCP. Qual è la sequenza corretta?
q.en: A host discovers skills from a server via Skills over MCP. What is the correct sequence?

o.it: resources/read di SKILL.md, che attiva subito la skill
o.en: resources/read of SKILL.md, which activates the skill at once

o.it: skills/list, verifica di digest SHA-256 e dimensione, approvazione, caricamento
o.en: skills/list, SHA-256 digest and size check, approval, loading

o.it: tools/call skill_install, poi riavvio del server
o.en: tools/call skill_install, then a server restart

o.it: prompts/get della skill, che il modello esegue subito
o.en: prompts/get of the skill, which the model runs at once

x.it: skills/list fornisce URI, digest SHA-256 e dimensione di ogni file. Leggere SKILL.md non attiva nulla: l'host carica la skill dopo verifica ed eventuale approvazione.
x.en: skills/list provides each file's URI, SHA-256 digest and size. Reading SKILL.md activates nothing: the host loads the skill after verification and any approval.

cite.text: A manifest MUST include `SKILL.md` and every supporting file, with each file's URI, SHA-256 digest, and byte size. Each entry returned by `skills/list` is complete; clients do not need to call `skills/get` for additional metadata.

q.it: Un tool ha una UI MCP Apps, ma il client non ha dichiarato l'estensione io.modelcontextprotocol/ui. Cosa ci si aspetta?
q.en: A tool has an MCP Apps UI, but the client did not declare the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui extension. What is expected?

o.it: Il server restituisce comunque il contenuto normale del tool
o.en: The server still returns the tool's normal content

o.it: Il server risponde -32021 a ogni chiamata del tool
o.en: The server answers -32021 to every call of the tool

o.it: Il client apre la risorsa ui:// in una nuova finestra
o.en: The client opens the ui:// resource in a new window

o.it: Il client esegue l'HTML direttamente nella pagina host
o.en: The client runs the HTML directly in the host page

x.it: Le estensioni sono opt-in con fallback al core: senza dichiarazione il tool funziona con il contenuto normale. Quando l'estensione c'è, la UI gira in un iframe sandboxed che comunica solo via postMessage.
x.en: Extensions are opt-in with fallback to core: without the declaration the tool works with normal content. When the extension is present, the UI runs in a sandboxed iframe communicating only via postMessage.

cite.text: If one party supports an extension but the other does not, the supporting party MUST either revert to core protocol behavior or reject the request with an appropriate error if the extension is mandatory. Extensions SHOULD document their expected fallback behavior. For example, a server offering UI-enhanced tools should still return meaningful text content for clients that do not support the UI extension, while a server requiring a specific authentication extension MAY reject connections from clients that do not support it.

q.it: Un host con 600 tool vuole ridurre token e dati sensibili nel contesto. Quali tecniche aiutano? (scegli 2)
q.en: A host with 600 tools wants to cut tokens and sensitive data in context. Which techniques help? (choose 2)

o.it: Progressive discovery: Catalog, Inspect, Execute
o.en: Progressive discovery: Catalog, Inspect, Execute

o.it: Caricare tutte le definizioni a ogni turno
o.en: Load every definition on each turn

o.it: Code mode: il modello scrive codice che chiama i tool in sandbox
o.en: Code mode: the model writes code that calls tools in a sandbox

o.it: Rimuovere inputSchema per accorciare le definizioni
o.en: Drop inputSchema to shorten definitions

x.it: Oltre l'1-5% del contesto conviene caricare le definizioni solo quando servono. Con code mode i risultati intermedi restano fuori dal contesto del modello.
x.en: Beyond 1-5% of context, load definitions only when needed. With code mode intermediate results stay out of the model's context.

cite.text: Progressive discovery and programmatic tool calling work well together. The model uses discovery tools to identify which tools it needs, loads their schemas, and then writes a single script that calls multiple tools in one execution pass. This combination minimizes both the token cost of tool definitions _and_ the token cost of tool results, keeping the model's context focused on reasoning rather than passing data through it.

q.it: Un server 2026-07-28 passa da 1 a 5 repliche dietro un load balancer round-robin. Cosa resta da fare? (scegli 2)
q.en: A 2026-07-28 server goes from 1 to 5 replicas behind a round-robin load balancer. What is left to do? (choose 2)

o.it: Configurare sticky sessions sull'Mcp-Session-Id
o.en: Configure sticky sessions on Mcp-Session-Id

o.it: Tenere lo stato degli handle in uno store condiviso
o.en: Keep handle state in a shared store

o.it: Autorizzare l'handle su ogni chiamata, legandolo all'utente
o.en: Authorize the handle on every call, bound to the user

o.it: Replicare la cache delle sessioni initialize
o.en: Replicate the initialize session cache

x.it: Il protocollo è stateless: niente sessioni né sticky routing. Lo stato applicativo dietro gli handle deve però essere raggiungibile da ogni replica, e ogni uso dell'handle va autorizzato.
x.en: The protocol is stateless: no sessions or sticky routing. The application state behind handles must however be reachable from every replica, and every handle use must be authorized.

cite.text: MCP has no protocol-level session, so a server cannot rely on implicit per-connection state to relate one tool call to the next. Servers that need to maintain state across calls — a shopping cart, an open browser context, a database transaction — should do so by returning an explicit handle from a creation tool and accepting that handle as an argument on subsequent calls.

q.it: Un team vuole distribuire un server locale a utenti non tecnici, con installazione in un clic su più client. Cosa usa?
q.en: A team wants to distribute a local server to non-technical users, with one-click install across several clients. What does it use?

o.it: Un bundle .mcpb con manifest.json
o.en: An .mcpb bundle with manifest.json

o.it: Un server.json con solo remotes
o.en: A server.json with remotes only

o.it: Un'estensione MCP Apps
o.en: An MCP Apps extension

o.it: Un link npx da incollare nel terminale
o.en: An npx link to paste in a terminal

x.it: MCPB (ex DXT) impacchetta server Node.js, Python o binari con un manifest.json obbligatorio, per l'installazione portabile tra client. Si può anche pubblicare nel registry con registryType mcpb.
x.en: MCPB (formerly DXT) packages Node.js, Python or binary servers with a required manifest.json, for portable install across clients. It can also be published to the registry with registryType mcpb.

cite.text: Servers: You can use MCPB to package your local MCP servers for distribution across multiple clients. The `mcpb` CLI helps you create a `manifest.json` and package your server into a `.mcpb` file. Once packaged, users can install your server with a single click in any client that supports MCP Bundles.

q.it: In un deployment remoto con gateway davanti al server, chi deve comunque autorizzare l'accesso a un handle specifico?
q.en: In a remote deployment with a gateway in front of the server, who must still authorize access to a specific handle?

o.it: Il gateway, filtrando su Mcp-Method
o.en: The gateway, filtering on Mcp-Method

o.it: Il server MCP, a ogni chiamata
o.en: The MCP server, on every call

o.it: L'authorization server, all'emissione del token
o.en: The authorization server, when issuing the token

o.it: L'host, mostrando una conferma all'utente
o.en: The host, by showing the user a confirmation

x.it: Il gateway filtra in modo grossolano sugli header; l'autorizzazione fine (incluso chi può usare quale handle) resta nel server a ogni chiamata.
x.en: The gateway filters coarsely on headers; fine-grained authorization (including who may use which handle) stays in the server on every call.

q.en: Without a shared protocol, an organization connecting N AI applications to M external systems must build and maintain roughly how many custom integrations?

o.en: M minus N separate integrations
N multiplied by M separate integrations
A single integration shared by every application
N plus M separate integrations

x.en: Each application-system pair needs its own custom connector without a shared protocol, so the integration count grows as N times M. A standard protocol like MCP turns that multiplicative cost into an additive N plus M relationship.

cite.text: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.

q.en: In MCP 2026-07-28, what may a server use to decide how to answer a new request?

o.en: The sequence of earlier calls made on the same connection
Assumptions carried over from the previous request it answered
The fields inside that request, plus any handle it names
A session object created when the connection was first opened

x.en: MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless: a server must treat each request as self-describing and must not infer identity, version, or capabilities from earlier traffic on the same connection. Any state that spans calls travels explicitly as a server-minted handle passed back as an argument.

cite.text: `_meta`: Carries the standard per-request fields: the protocol version and client capabilities that every MCP request must include, plus the client's identity, which clients should include unless configured not to.

q.en: A client sends a request and receives UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. What should it do next?

o.en: Resend the identical unchanged request and simply wait for a new result
Fall back permanently to the older 2024-11-05 initialize handshake flow
Close the connection permanently and refuse to contact that server again
Retry the request once using a version from the error's supported list

x.en: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError carries the versions the server supports in its data, so a client negotiates by retrying with one of those values rather than guessing, giving up, or assuming a legacy handshake is required.

cite.text: The client SHOULD select a mutually supported version from the `supported` list and retry the request, or surface an error to the user if no compatible version exists.

q.en: In the MCP specification's use of RFC 2119 keywords, what does a requirement written with MUST mean for an implementation?

o.en: The behavior is mandatory, and non-conformant implementations fail
The behavior is recommended but implementations may reasonably skip it
The behavior is one optional idea among several equally valid designs
The behavior is only a suggestion for future specification drafts

x.en: RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 define MUST as an absolute requirement. Reading requirement strength correctly separates mandatory behavior from SHOULD recommendations and MAY options, which is essential for interpreting any specification clause precisely.

cite.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

q.en: Which two statements correctly describe MCP's JSON-RPC message shapes? Select two.

o.en: Several requests may still be batched together inside one array
A request's id must be non-null and cannot repeat a still-pending id
A result response may safely omit resultType whenever a server prefers
A notification never carries an id and never gets a reply

x.en: A notification has no id and the receiver must never answer it, while a request id must be non-null and must not repeat while an earlier request with that id is still awaiting a response. Batching was removed, and a modern result must include resultType.

cite.text: Requests are sent from the client to the server, to initiate an operation.: Requests MUST include a string or integer ID.

q.en: A tool definition omits its annotations object entirely. Under the default values, how should a client treat that tool?

o.en: As destructive, read-only, idempotent, and closed-world
As destructive, not read-only, not idempotent, and open-world
As non-destructive, non-idempotent, closed-world, and read-only
As read-only, non-destructive, idempotent, and closed-world

x.en: When annotations are omitted, the defaults apply: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, and openWorldHint true. Clients must treat these as untrusted hints from the server, not enforced guarantees, when deciding whether to prompt for confirmation.

cite.text: ToolAnnotations: readOnlyHint (Default: false); destructiveHint: If true, the tool may perform destructive updates to its environment (Default: true); idempotentHint (Default: false); openWorldHint (Default: true).

q.en: A server publishes a tool that takes no parameters. Which inputSchema value is correct for that tool under 2026-07-28?

o.en: An empty JSON array standing in for the schema
A null value marking the tool as taking no arguments
An object schema with type object and additionalProperties false
Leaving inputSchema absent from the tool definition entirely

x.en: inputSchema is never null and is never left out; a tool that takes no parameters still declares an object schema, conventionally type object with additionalProperties false, so only an empty arguments object validates against it.

cite.text: `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }` - accepts only empty objects `{}`

q.en: Which two statements correctly describe how a host manages connections to multiple MCP servers? Select two.

o.en: Colliding tool names from different servers are disambiguated with a server prefix
A server's self-reported serverInfo.name is guaranteed unique for routing
One client instance is shared across every server connection
The host embeds a separate client for each server connection

x.en: A host binds one client to each server so responsibilities and trust stay separated, and it commonly prefixes tool names by server identifier to resolve collisions, since serverInfo is self-reported and not guaranteed unique.

cite.text: Tool name uniqueness is scoped to a single server. Clients or proxies that aggregate tools from multiple servers MAY encounter naming collisions (for example, two servers each exposing a `search` tool) and SHOULD implement a disambiguation strategy such as prefixing tool names with a server identifier.

q.en: A tool call returns a result with isError true because the arguments failed validation. What should the host do with that result?

o.en: Silently drop the call without ever informing the model
Treat it exactly like a protocol error and stop all retries
Discard the conversation and restart the request from scratch
Feed the error content back so the model can retry correctly

x.en: Tool execution errors are ordinary results carrying isError and explanatory content, designed to flow back into the model's context so the model can revise its arguments and try again, unlike a protocol-level failure.

cite.text: Clients MAY provide protocol errors to language models, though these are less likely to result in successful recovery. Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.

q.en: A client answers an input_required result from a tools/call request. How should it send its answers back to the server?

o.en: Retry the same request with a new id and matching requestState
Open a brand-new elicitation/create request completely on its own
Reply by reusing the original request id the server first saw
Send it as a notification, since no server reply is expected

x.en: Multi round-trip requests require the retry to carry a new JSON-RPC id along with inputResponses and the requestState echoed exactly as received; reusing the old id or inventing a fresh state value breaks the round trip.

cite.text: The JSON-RPC `id` MUST be different between the initial request and the retry, as they are independent requests.

q.en: What must be the first message a server sends after accepting a subscriptions/listen request?

o.en: A progress notification carrying the newly assigned subscriptionId
An acknowledged message naming the filters the server will honor
The first list_changed notification that happens to be pending
An empty result that closes the stream right after it opens

x.en: The stream must open with an acknowledgment naming the subset of requested notification types the server will actually honor, before any list-changed or resource-updated events, so the client knows exactly what it will receive.

cite.text: The server MUST send `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged` as the first message carrying the subscription's ID in `_meta` under `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`, and MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before it. On stdio, where every subscription shares one channel, this ordering is defined per subscription ID and not per channel: messages belonging to other subscriptions MAY be interleaved before it.

q.en: Which two statements are true about the tasks extension in 2026-07-28? Select two.

o.en: A client polls task progress by repeatedly calling tasks/list
tasks/cancel asks the server to stop cooperatively, not instantly
A client must declare the extension before a server returns a task
Tasks belong to the required core protocol every server implements

x.en: Tasks moved out of the core protocol into an opt-in extension, so a server only returns a task result when the client has declared support, the client polls with tasks/get rather than a list method, and cancellation is cooperative rather than instant.

cite.text: Cancellation. The client can send `tasks/cancel` at any time. Cancellation is cooperative — the server acknowledges the intent but is not obligated to stop the work.

q.en: An unknown tool name, an invalid prompt name, and a missing required prompt argument all map to which JSON-RPC error code in 2026-07-28?

o.en: -32021, because the client is missing a required capability
-32601, because each names a method the server does not recognize
-32602, because each is an invalid-parameters failure before any execution
-32002, the legacy not-found code every current server should still emit

x.en: All three failures are recognized before any tool or prompt runs, so 2026-07-28 groups them under Invalid params rather than treating them as unknown methods, legacy not-found errors, or a missing client capability.

cite.text: A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code `-32602` (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be `400 Bad Request`.

q.en: An HTTP request's Mcp-Method header names tools/call, but the JSON body's method field says prompts/get. What should the server do?

o.en: Merge both methods and attempt to satisfy each partially
Process the request as tools/call because headers take precedence
Trust the JSON body and silently ignore the header value
Reject it with -32020 because the header disagrees with the body

x.en: Required headers exist so gateways can route without parsing bodies, so a server must reject a request whose header disagrees with its body using the HeaderMismatch code rather than picking one side or blending both methods.

cite.text: Any server that processes the message body MUST validate that encoded header values, after decoding if Base64-encoded, match the corresponding values in the request body. Servers MUST reject requests with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status and JSON-RPC error code `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) if any validation fails.

q.en: A tool call's Streamable HTTP response stream breaks before a result arrives. What is the correct recovery?

o.en: Reissue the same call as a new request with a new id
Treat the broken stream as a successful empty result
Abandon the tool entirely and remove it from the tool list
Wait indefinitely on the same stream since the result is still coming

x.en: A broken stream loses whatever response was in flight, and since MCP dropped stream resumability, the only correct recovery is reissuing the call as a fresh request with a new id rather than waiting forever or assuming success.

cite.text: Remove SSE stream resumability and message redelivery (the `Last-Event-ID` header and SSE event IDs) from the Streamable HTTP transport. A broken response stream loses the in-flight request; clients MUST re-issue it as a new request with a new request ID (SEP-2575).

q.en: Which two features are deprecated but still functional in MCP 2026-07-28? Select two.

o.en: Roots, reached now through a multi round-trip input request
Sampling, reached now through a multi round-trip input request
The subscriptions/listen request used to open a notification stream
The server/discover request every server must implement

x.en: Roots and sampling were deprecated in 2026-07-28 but keep working through multi round-trip input requests of type roots/list and sampling/createMessage, unlike server/discover and subscriptions/listen, which remain current, non-deprecated parts of the core protocol.

cite.text: When a server needs client input (sampling, elicitation, or roots) to complete a request, it answers with an `InputRequiredResult` and the client retries the request with the matching `inputResponses`. See Multi Round-Trip Requests.

q.en: A resources/read result is marked cacheScope public. What does that scope actually control?

o.en: Whether the server enforces access control before returning the resource
Whether the cached entry may be shared across different users and tokens
Whether the resource content itself is readable by any user
Whether the underlying file on disk is writable by the client

x.en: cacheScope only governs whether a cached response may be reused across different callers; it is never an access-control mechanism, so a server must still authorize every read independent of whether the result happens to be publicly cacheable.

cite.text: A `cacheScope` of `"public"` indicates that the response does not contain user-specific data and can be safely shared. Servers MUST be aware that responses with a `"public"` `cacheScope` may be shared between callers even if the Result is coming from an authenticated endpoint. For example, the Result from an authenticated `tools/list` call with a `"public"` `cacheScope` may be cached by a client and may be shared outside of the initial request's authorization context (i.e. different access tokens can leverage the same cache).

q.en: A server's discover result reports serverInfo with a trustworthy-sounding name. What role may serverInfo correctly play?

o.en: Proof that the server's tool descriptions are safe to trust
Granting that server elevated access without further checks
Display and logging only, never an authorization decision
A substitute for validating the server's OAuth token audience

x.en: clientInfo and serverInfo are self-reported fields meant for display, logging, and debugging. A host must never use them to grant access, vouch for tool safety, or replace audience validation, since any server can claim any name.

cite.text: `serverInfo` is self-reported by the server and is not verified by the protocol. It is intended for display, logging, and debugging. Clients SHOULD NOT use it to change their behavior, and SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions.

q.en: An authorization server's metadata does not list code_challenge_methods_supported. What must a compliant MCP client do?

o.en: Fall back to sending the client secret in the URL
Assume S256 support and continue the flow as normal
Proceed without PKCE since the field is optional for legacy servers
Refuse to proceed with authorization against that server

x.en: PKCE is mandatory for every MCP authorization flow, so when an authorization server does not advertise its supported challenge methods the client cannot confirm PKCE support and must refuse to continue rather than guessing or skipping it.

cite.text: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata: If `code_challenge_methods_supported` is absent, the authorization server does not support PKCE and MCP clients MUST refuse to proceed.

q.en: An MCP client has no pre-registered credentials, and the authorization server advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported. What should it try next?

o.en: Register using a Client ID Metadata Document at an HTTPS URL
Wait for the server to push credentials to the client
Skip straight to Dynamic Client Registration since it is fastest
Ask the end user to type in a client id manually

x.en: The registration priority places pre-registration first, then Client ID Metadata Documents whenever the authorization server advertises support for them, ahead of the deprecated Dynamic Client Registration path and asking the user as a last resort.

cite.text: MCP clients and authorization servers SHOULD support OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents as specified in OAuth Client ID Metadata Document for client registration.

q.en: A request fails with 403 and error insufficient_scope, listing three required scopes the client never held. What should the client request on retry?

o.en: The same original scope set, unchanged, retried again until it works
The union of its earlier granted scopes and the newly required ones
Every scope the authorization server has ever defined, just to be safe
Only the three newly required scopes, dropping what it already held

x.en: Step-up authorization asks for the union of the client's prior scopes and the scopes named in the challenge, within a limited number of retries, so access grows precisely rather than shrinking, over-requesting, or repeating an insufficient request unchanged.

cite.text: Step-up: the request needs scopes the current token doesn't carry. The Inspector re-authorizes for the union of the held and required scopes, so the new token covers everything the old one did plus the newly required scopes.

q.en: Which two practices help a host defend against a tool definition changing maliciously after a user first approved it? Select two.

o.en: Trusting every list_changed notification as automatically re-approved
Disabling tools/list caching entirely so nothing is ever pinned
Treating a changed listing as a rug pull until it is re-reviewed
Pinning approved tool definitions and reviewing any change before reuse

x.en: A rug pull happens when a previously approved tool's definition drifts silently, so defenses pin the approved definition and hold any change for re-review rather than auto-trusting every update or abandoning caching altogether, which would not by itself detect drift.

q.en: A request carries traceparent in its _meta and calls through to an upstream system. What should happen to that trace context?

o.en: It is stored only in server logs and never forwarded onward
It is regenerated at every hop so each hop gets a new trace
It propagates through the call chain so spans share one trace id
It is discarded once the request leaves the originating client

x.en: W3C Trace Context fields such as traceparent are meant to propagate across the whole call chain so that spans in the host, client, server, and any upstream system can be correlated under one shared trace id for observability.

cite.text: As an exception to the prefix requirement above, the keys `traceparent`, `tracestate`, and `baggage` are reserved for OpenTelemetry trace context propagation. When present, their values MUST follow W3C Trace Context and W3C Baggage formats respectively.

q.en: An audit log needs to prove that no earlier record was altered after the fact. What technique gives that tamper evidence?

o.en: Encrypting the log so only an administrator can open the file
Rotating the log file each day and deleting the old copies
Storing every record in a plain text file with no structure
Chaining each record's checksum to the one stored before it

x.en: A hash chain links each audit record to the hash of its predecessor, so altering or removing any earlier entry breaks the chain and is detectable, which plain storage, rotation, or encryption alone do not guarantee.

q.en: A proposed change to the MCP specification has been merged as a Final SEP, and its deprecation window has now elapsed. Who decides to actually remove that feature?

o.en: The Core Maintainers, after the minimum deprecation window has passed
An automated script once the deprecation window elapses
Any single contributor who opens a pull request
The end users of the AI application, by majority vote

x.en: The feature lifecycle sets a minimum deprecation window, but reaching that window only makes removal eligible; the Core Maintainers still decide when a deprecated feature is actually removed, rather than an individual contributor, a vote, or automation.

cite.text: After the minimum deprecation window has elapsed, Core Maintainers may remove the feature when preparing a release. The removal is recorded in `changelog.mdx` under the "Removed" heading and in the registry. Any change to the original deprecation or removal, such as extending or shortening the timeline (Expedited removal) or restoring the feature to Active (Feature states), requires a SEP. A feature may remain Deprecated indefinitely.

q.en: A team deploys an MCP server that runs as a local stdio subprocess. Whose responsibility is it to supply that server's credentials?

o.en: The model, which requests them through a tool call
The operator, who provides them through the local environment
The end user, typed into the model's chat window
The authorization server, through a browser redirect flow

x.en: stdio servers should not run the OAuth browser flow and instead read credentials from the environment the operator controls, which is a deployment responsibility distinct from asking the end user directly or routing credentials through the model or a redirect.

cite.text: The OAuth flow in this guide is for HTTP-based transports. Servers that use the stdio transport should retrieve credentials from the environment instead. They run locally, so they can also use credentials from libraries embedded in the server.

q.en: Which three recommendations correctly match a use case to its fitting MCP mechanism? Select three.

o.en: A read of one user's private data should cache with a private cacheScope
A user-initiated slash-command template should be exposed as a tool
A multi-minute build job should use the tasks extension
A machine-to-machine integration with no human present should use the client credentials extension

x.en: Long jobs fit the tasks extension, unattended service-to-service calls fit the client credentials authorization extension, and private per-user reads should cache with a private scope; a user-triggered template belongs to the user-controlled prompts primitive, not tools.

cite.text: `cacheScope` = `"private"` | Only the requesting user's client MAY cache. Shared caches MUST NOT serve a cached copy to a different user.

q.en: In the MCP Apps extension, a tool's _meta.ui object carries resourceUri together with which other field?

o.en: csp, listing which domains the rendered iframe may contact
domain, naming the origin that the UI resource is served from
visibility, controlling whether the model or the app may call it
permissions, granting the iframe access to a camera or microphone

x.en: A tool's _meta.ui carries resourceUri plus visibility, which defaults to both model and app; a host must not list the tool to the model when visibility lacks model, and must reject an app-originated call when it lacks app. The csp, permissions, and domain fields describe the UI resource itself, not the tool.

q.en: A third party wants to define a new MCP extension identifier. Which form is correct under the naming rules?

o.en: Any string at all, since extension names are not validated
A single word with no domain or prefix at all
The reserved io.modelcontextprotocol prefix, used for any extension author
A reversed domain the author owns, such as com.example/my-extension

x.en: Extension identifiers follow the _meta naming rules: official extensions use io.modelcontextprotocol, while third parties must use a reversed domain they actually own, so a single unvalidated word or the reserved official prefix would both be incorrect choices.

cite.text: To prevent identifier collisions, the vendor prefix SHOULD be a reversed domain name that the extension author owns or controls (similar to Java package naming conventions). For example, a company owning `example.com` would use `com.example/` as their prefix.

q.en: What percentage of the conformance test suite must an SDK pass to qualify for Tier 1?

o.en: A full one hundred percent, plus very early feature delivery
Fifty percent, with the remainder scheduled for a later release
Sixty percent, matching the floor set for any listed SDK
Eighty percent, the same bar that Tier 2 must clear

x.en: Tier 1 is the strongest SDK tier: it requires passing the full conformance suite, shipping features before the related spec release, and meeting fast triage and bug-fix windows, which is a stricter bar than the eighty percent required for Tier 2.

cite.text: Tier 1 SDKs are fully supported and implement every non-experimental feature, including optional capabilities such as sampling and elicitation. SDKs in Tier 2 are actively maintained and working toward full specification support, and those in Tier 3 are experimental, partially implemented, or specialized. Experimental features and protocol extensions (such as Tasks and MCP Apps) are not required for any tier.

q.en: A platform team currently maintains a separate hand-written connector between each of six internal applications and nine external systems, and the number of connectors keeps growing as new applications and systems are added. Leadership asks whether adopting one shared protocol like MCP for context and tool access would help. What is the strongest justification?

o.en: MCP turns the multiplicative growth of custom connectors into an additive one across compliant applications and systems
MCP replaces the need for any authorization or consent step between an application and the systems it reaches
MCP guarantees every external system will expose identical data regardless of what that system actually stores
MCP removes the need for the team to ever choose which specific large language model an application uses internally today

x.en: MCP standardizes the integration surface between AI applications and external systems, so growth changes from roughly the count of applications times systems to roughly their sum. It does not choose models, guarantee identical data, or remove authorization requirements.

cite.text: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools. Whether you're building an AI-powered IDE, enhancing a chat interface, or creating custom AI workflows, MCP provides a standardized way to connect LLMs with the context they need.

q.en: A support engineer who is new to the team tells a colleague that every MCP exchange must open with an initialize request before the server will accept any other call. The colleague is reviewing the 2026-07-28 specification. How should the colleague respond?

o.en: Agree, because initialize still creates the shared session that every later request in the exchange truly depends on
Explain that initialize and sessions were removed, since every request now carries its own version and capabilities
Agree, but note that only remote HTTP servers still require the complete initialize handshake today
Explain that initialize is now considered fully optional but still returns a session id for later calls

x.en: The 2026-07-28 revision removed the initialize request and notifications/initialized along with protocol sessions. Every request instead carries protocolVersion, clientCapabilities, and related fields in its own per-request metadata, so no handshake or session is required.

cite.text: MCP is a stateless protocol. Every request carries the protocol version and the capabilities relevant to that request in its `_meta` field, so the server can process each request on its own. Clients should also identify themselves in the same field unless configured not to. Servers advertise their supported versions and capabilities through the mandatory `server/discover` request, which clients may send before any other request. Detailed information can be found in the specification, and the example showcases the per-request metadata and the discovery sequence.

q.en: A team is deciding whether it is still safe to rely on the roots feature in a client they are building. One engineer says the feature was removed in 2026-07-28 and must be deleted immediately. Another checks the deprecated features registry. What does the registry actually show for a deprecated feature like roots?

o.en: It is undocumented, so the team must simply guess its status from forum posts
It is Active and considered fully current, so no change is required for years right now
It is Deprecated, still functional, with a migration path and an earliest removal date
It is Removed already, so any client code that calls it will fail immediately

x.en: The feature lifecycle keeps a deprecated feature specified and working, with a required migration path and a minimum window before removal is even possible. Confusing deprecated with removed causes teams to delete working integrations too early.

cite.text: Feature | Deprecation SEP | Deprecated in | Migration path | Earliest removal

q.en: An operator scales a remote MCP server from one replica to three behind a load balancer with no sticky routing. A tool that kept a per-client running total in process memory starts returning totals that jump around between calls. What is the root cause?

o.en: The load balancer is rewriting JSON-RPC ids, so results get matched to the wrong calls
The client stopped declaring capabilities after its first call, so later replicas ignore it
Each replica negotiates its own protocol version, so replicas disagree on the result format
The total lived in one replica's memory, so replicas that never saw it cannot continue it

x.en: Under the stateless core every request must be answerable from its own contents plus any explicit handle it names, so state that spans calls belongs behind a server-minted handle backed by shared storage, not in one replica's memory. Once requests spread across replicas, implicit per-client memory is invisible to the replicas that did not create it, which is exactly the drift the operator sees.

cite.text: MCP has no protocol-level session, so a server cannot rely on implicit per-connection state to relate one tool call to the next. Servers that need to maintain state across calls — a shopping cart, an open browser context, a database transaction — should do so by returning an explicit handle from a creation tool and accepting that handle as an argument on subsequent calls.

q.en: A developer who previously built JSON-RPC batch clients wants to send several tool calls in one HTTP POST body to a 2026-07-28 server to save round trips. What should the developer expect?

o.en: The request is rejected, since batching was removed and each POST body now carries exactly one request
The server processes only the first call in the array and silently drops the rest
The server happily accepts the whole batch and answers each call inside one large combined result array
The server queues the extra calls and answers them one at a time over minutes

x.en: JSON-RPC batching was removed from MCP in the 2025-06-18 revision and remains absent in 2026-07-28, so a Streamable HTTP POST body must contain exactly one JSON-RPC request or notification rather than an array of several.

cite.text: Every JSON-RPC message sent from the client MUST be a new HTTP POST request to the MCP endpoint.

q.en: A new teammate asks how a host relates to the clients and servers it works with. Which description matches the 2026-07-28 architecture?

o.en: The host is a single client that multiplexes every server connection over one shared common channel
The host embeds one client per server connection, and each client talks to exactly one server
Each server embeds its own client to reach the host directly
Clients and servers connect to each other directly, with the host present only for billing

x.en: A host application embeds one client instance per server connection, so each client maintains a one to one relationship with a single server while the host coordinates the overall set of connections and aggregates their results for the model.

cite.text: MCP follows a client-server architecture where an MCP host — an AI application like Claude Code or Claude Desktop — establishes connections to one or more MCP servers. The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server. Each MCP client maintains a dedicated connection with its corresponding MCP server.

q.en: A vendor proposes that the company build one bespoke SDK per partner system instead of adopting MCP, arguing that a shared protocol adds unnecessary abstraction. What is the strongest counterpoint grounded in interoperability?

o.en: A shared protocol means partner systems no longer need to publish any documentation at all
A shared protocol removes the need to ever negotiate a protocol version again
A shared protocol lets any compliant client use any compliant server without system-specific glue code
A shared protocol supposedly guarantees every single partner system will have identical performance results

x.en: The value of one open protocol is that discovery and capability negotiation are data rather than code, so a client built once can work with any conforming server. It does not equalize performance, remove version negotiation, or replace documentation.

cite.text: MCP takes some inspiration from the Language Server Protocol, which standardizes how to add support for programming languages across a whole ecosystem of development tools. In a similar way, MCP standardizes how to integrate additional context and tools into the ecosystem of AI applications.

q.en: An architecture review is listing the real benefits of adopting one open protocol like MCP instead of custom point-to-point integrations. Which two statements are accurate? Select two.

o.en: The specific model that the host application uses internally no longer needs to be chosen or configured at all
Every server automatically inherits the exact same user interface as every other connected server today
Any modern client can use any modern server without integration-specific code, because discovery is expressed as data
Growth in the number of connectors becomes additive across applications and systems instead of multiplicative

x.en: Standardizing the wire between applications and systems lets a client discover and use any compliant server without bespoke glue code, turning multiplicative integration growth into additive growth. MCP does not standardize user interfaces or choose which model a host runs.

cite.text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) follows a client-host-server architecture where each host can run multiple client instances. MCP is a stateless protocol: every request is self-contained and carries its own protocol version and capabilities. This architecture enables users to integrate AI capabilities across applications while maintaining clear security boundaries and isolating concerns. Built on JSON-RPC, MCP provides a protocol focused on context exchange between clients and servers.

q.en: While reading a changelog entry for the 2026-07-28 revision, an engineer sees a line that references a specific SEP number and a short headline. What is the correct way to use that entry to judge whether a feature is safe to build against today?

o.en: Ignore the changelog entirely and rely only on the previous revision's own documentation
Treat the changelog headline alone as fully sufficient, since SEP numbers are only historical trivia anyway
Assume every single changelog entry describes a feature that is now already removed
Look up the referenced SEP and the current specification page to confirm the feature's lifecycle stage

x.en: A changelog entry names what changed and links to the proposal that drove it, but the authoritative status of a feature is its current lifecycle stage on the specification and deprecated-features pages, which the reader should confirm directly rather than guessing from the headline.

q.en: A team is documenting why their MCP server design keeps every request self-contained instead of relying on connection state. Which two consequences follow from that stateless design? Select two.

o.en: Any replica behind a load balancer can correctly answer any incoming request
The server can skip declaring resultType because the connection already establishes what kind of answer to expect
A dropped and retried request can be routed to a different server instance without breaking correctness
The server may safely infer a client's identity from an earlier request on the same connection

x.en: Because no information may carry over from a prior request on the same connection, any replica can serve any request and a retry is safe to route anywhere, which is exactly why load balancers need no stickiness under the stateless core.

cite.text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a stateless protocol: all the information needed to process a request is contained in the request itself. A server processes each request independently; no state should be inferred from previous requests, even those on the same connection or stream.

q.en: A client sends a tools/call request for a tool whose description says it may ask the user follow-up questions, but the client's request never declared the elicitation capability. What should the server do?

o.en: Answer with a MissingRequiredClientCapability error naming the capability the client must declare
Silently downgrade the entire tool call to a safer read-only variant instead
Cache the request indefinitely until the client eventually declares the missing capability itself
Proceed anyway regardless, since capability declarations are only a minor formality

x.en: A server must not rely on a capability the client did not declare on that specific request, so when it needs elicitation and the request lacks that capability, it returns the MissingRequiredClientCapability error with the required capabilities listed in the error data.

cite.text: A server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared. If processing a request requires a capability the client did not declare in its `clientCapabilities`, the server MUST return a JSON-RPC error specifying the missing capabilities. For HTTP, the response status code MUST be `400 Bad Request`.

q.en: A tool defines an outputSchema describing a structured invoice object. A client calls the tool and receives a result with structuredContent that does not match that schema. What does this indicate about the server's implementation?

o.en: The client must have sent an incorrectly formed inputSchema along with the original call
The server violated its own contract, since structuredContent must conform to a declared outputSchema
Nothing at all, because outputSchema is only decorative and is never checked against the actual result
The mismatch is expected whenever a tool also happens to return a text content block

x.en: When a tool declares an outputSchema, any structuredContent the server returns must conform to it, and the server should also serialize the same data into a text block for compatibility. A mismatch is a defect in the server's tool implementation, not a client error.

cite.text: Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema.
